ratings_why.fun: A windable clock plus positional text-borrowing gives real shop puzzles every turn (Leveret behind Old Wat with Almanac Jill, a Jack left of The Three Hares), held back from 8 by the readability load and some plain buffers.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because no tribe today uses other tribes' printed text: Borrow makes the Hares a doubling layer for whatever you run, timed by a moon the opponent can see.

verdict_why: Grandam of the Forms fires on New Moon, but Leverets only borrow while the moon is Full, so her capstone line doesn't work as written.

points.text: Grandam of the Forms fires on New Moon, when no Leveret is borrowing anything (Borrow is Full-only). Say "each Leveret whose Borrow target is a Hare", or the Dark of the moon build and the second-Scour high roll fall apart.

Leverets borrowing sell text, plus Old Wat and Almanac Jill, give a Leveret that comes back each turn and turns the moon twice for free. That's the best hidden combo here; keep it and show it in a build.
Waning only feeds the Dusk Nurse. A Waning card that keeps borrowed text one phase longer would turn "step past Full" into its own combo choice.
Spring Jill and the Hare's-Foot Charmer do one obvious job. A small hook, like Spring Jill turning the moon when her Bristle kills, would tie the early game into the clock.
Witch in Borrowed Shape plus Moon-Caller flipping Full mid-fight is a great surprise; a Moonlit line on Moon-Caller itself would make that fight line easier to draft into.

standouts.why: Ribboned Jack is a two-card puzzle with every neighbour, Hare or not, and makes slot order matter.
The Three Hares multiplies every permanent buff and stacks with a Jack that borrows it, the kind of overlap a combo player hunts for.
Old Wat is a reusable moon turner that a Leveret or Jack can copy, so one card feeds three builds.

weakest.why: Ring Referee is a plain team buffer with nothing to combine with beyond more Full Moons.
Hare's-Foot Charmer is a generic adjacency buff; only a Jack or The Three Hares makes it interesting.
Spring Jill is a fine body with no link to the rest of the tribe's engines.

flags.note: "Leveret borrowing a Hare" on New Moon contradicts Borrow being Full-only.
Created copies that count towards triples, doubled by Dame Waxwell, are the likeliest runaway.
Sister Silverpenny copies another tribe's Tier 6 capstone at any phase from Tier 5.
Golden Dame Waxwell with Mother Meikle Care and The Moon-Scour stacks fast; needs a ceiling sim.
Leverets borrowing Old Wat's sell text give free moon turns every turn; capped only by back-row space.
